content.subject: Power Electronics
content.hook: Why does removing the gate pulse still turn off your thyristor?
content.question: Which statement correctly compares latching current and holding current in a thyristor?
options: Latching current is greater than holding current and associates with turn on
Holding current is greater than latching current and associates with turn on
Latching current is less than holding current and associates with turn off
Holding current is equal to latching current and associates with turn off
content.answerLine: Latching current is greater than holding current and associates with turn on.
explanation: Latching current is the minimum anode current needed to maintain conduction right after gate removal.
If the anode current fails to reach latching level, the SCR turns off immediately.
Holding current is the minimum anode current below which an operating thyristor drops into off state.
Therefore latching current is associated with turning on, while holding current is associated with turn off.
content.funFact: Because latching current exceeds holding current, inductive loads require wider gate pulses to ensure proper turn-on.
content.outro: Remember, latching means turn on, holding means turn off. Subscribe for more electrical engineering exam prep!

script.narration: Latching current is the minimum anode current needed to maintain conduction right after gate removal.
If the anode current fails to reach latching level, the SCR turns off immediately.
Holding current is the minimum anode current below which an operating thyristor drops into off state.
Therefore latching current is associated with turning on, while holding current is associated with turn off.
In standard silicon controlled rectifiers, latching current is typically two to three times the holding current.
Remember the simple alphabetical memory aid: L comes after H, so latching current is always higher.
If load current rises to fifty milliamperes, an SCR with sixty milliampere latching current turns off.
To turn the device off successfully, anode current must be forced completely below the holding value.
State AE and JE papers test this fundamental relationship frequently because candidates often swap the definitions.
